summary: Cosmic Atlas is a macOS workbench for investigating environmental change across Sri Lanka. It brings NASA Earth science data into an interactive map and timeline so users can choose a variable, compare locations and see how strongly the records support a trend. At 25 representative sample sites, Atlas shows the rate of change, uncertainty and statistical significance. In our daily high temperature example, the Jaffna sample warmed by an estimated 0.30 °C per decade from January 2004 to October 2026, while the Colombo result was inconclusive. Users can export the findings as PDF or CSV. A separate 3D weather view uses NOAA guidance for short-range planning.
details:
Cosmic Atlas addresses Be an Earth System Trend Detective! by combining Earth science data, visualization and statistical analysis in one native macOS app. Trend Detective lets users choose a variable, date range and sample site, compare two locations, and switch between raw monthly records and a series adjusted for seasonality. The bundled archive covers 25 representative Sri Lankan grid samples and up to 11 variables, including rainfall, air temperature, wind, soil wetness and solar radiation. NASA POWER supplies the historical numeric data, including GPM IMERG precipitation and NASA reanalysis meteorology.

Atlas estimates rates of change per decade with a linear regression that accounts for the calendar month. It uses Newey–West standard errors and Holm-adjusted tests across eligible sites. For January 2004 to October 2026, the Jaffna daily-high-temperature sample showed +0.30 °C per decade (95% interval +0.15 to +0.45, Holm-adjusted p = 0.003). Colombo's +0.14 °C per decade was inconclusive (95% interval −0.15 to +0.43). These are separate tests against zero at representative grid points. The app shows coverage and coordinates, compares against NOAA station records where available, and exports the chart and findings as PDF or the underlying series as CSV.

The app uses Swift and SwiftUI for its interface and analysis, CesiumJS in WebKit for interactive mapping, and Python for data preparation and model training. The bundled trend analysis and local model inference run on the user's Mac. The 3D Weather view and project planner use separate NOAA GFS forecasts from Open-Meteo for short-range planning. AI assisted development and drafting. The optional Ask Atlas feature uses OpenAI for question routing. The reported trends come from the archived data and statistical analysis.
